title: [VSC-14] VS Code: read-only Accounts view in the Moe sidebar
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0). Depends on VSC-13 (task-065e4812d96247cc8394b3cd0416475d: moe-vscode/src/util/AccountPresentation.ts), which itself depends on VSC-12 (the client's accountRotation and onAccountsChanged) and VSC-7 (the accounts corpus).

Objective: show Claude account rotation in VS Code the way JetBrains' Accounts tab lists it (moe-jetbrains AccountsPanel.kt): one item per AccountPresentation row, the chips line, and an empty or disconnected state, refreshed on onAccountsChanged and on connection changes. Read-only in this row.

Deliverable: new moe-vscode/src/providers/AccountsTreeProvider.ts (a TreeDataProvider modelled on ManagedVmTreeProvider.ts); moe-vscode/package.json gains a "moe.accounts" view in the moe views container and a "moe.accounts.refresh" command with a view/title entry; moe-vscode/src/extension.ts registers both; new moe-vscode/tests/accounts-view.test.cjs drives the provider under node:vm with a fake vscode and a fake client.

Not in scope: add, remove, move, rename, switch-percent and sign-in actions (VSC-15), any MoeDaemonClient.ts change, any moe-jetbrains file.

Verification (GLOBAL rail: never npm in the shared checkout): `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo into a fresh directory outside the checkout, overlay this task's files, then in <snapshot>/moe-vscode run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` under `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl).
definitionOfDone: moe-vscode/package.json declares the moe.accounts view in the moe views container and the moe.accounts.refresh command with a view/title entry for that view, and tests/accounts-view.test.cjs asserts both from package.json.

With a fake client holding a two-account rotation, the provider's getChildren returns one item per AccountPresentation row, in row order, with labels and descriptions resolved to the MoeBundle English.

Firing onAccountsChanged or onConnectionChanged makes the provider fire onDidChangeTreeData; a disconnected client or a null rotation yields the single empty-state item; dispose() removes every listener it added.
moe-vscode/src/extension.ts registers the provider and the refresh command and pushes both disposables into context.subscriptions.
In a git-archive snapshot of HEAD plus this diff, `cd moe-vscode && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` exits 0 with 0 failures.

Built on HEAD b863458a (VSC-13 landed). tests/accounts-corpus.test.cjs (plain node --test) 5/5 green, so check (b) pins the new keys to the bundle. 24 dirty peer paths untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
Create moe-vscode/src/providers/AccountsTreeProvider.ts with the Write tool, modelled on ManagedVmTreeProvider.ts.
Imports:
- `import * as vscode from 'vscode'`;
- `import type { MoeDaemonClient } from '../services/MoeDaemonClient'`. It MUST be type-only, so the test's require map stays at vscode plus AccountPresentation;
- a value import of chips, parseAccountRotation, resolveAccountText and rows from '../util/AccountPresentation'.
Declarations:
- `type AccountsClient = Pick<MoeDaemonClient, 'connectionState' | 'isStateReady' | 'accountRotation' | 'onAccountsChanged' | 'onConnectionChanged' | 'onStateChanged'>`. accountRotation and onAccountsChanged come from VSC-12, task-daf5abdd, whose DoD names them.
- `const SEPARATOR = '  ·  '` (JetBrains AccountPresentation.SEPARATOR).
- `const text = (key, ...args) => resolveAccountText({ key, args })`.
- Exported class AccountsTreeProvider implements vscode.TreeDataProvider<AccountNode> and vscode.Disposable, where AccountNode = { label; description?; tooltip?; id?; contextValue? }.
Constructor `(client: AccountsClient, clock = { now: () => Date.now(), zone: () => Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone || 'UTC' })`:
- it subscribes client.onAccountsChanged, client.onConnectionChanged and client.onStateChanged, each calling refresh();
- onStateChanged matters because a STATE_SNAPSHOT flips isStateReady and may carry the first rotation.
parts(): { items: AccountNode[]; description?: string; message?: string }, mirroring JetBrains AccountsPanel.render:
1. connectionState !== 'connected' gives [{ label: text('moe.accounts.notConnected') }].
2. rotation = parseAccountRotation(client.accountRotation). When it is null: [{ label: text(client.isStateReady ? 'moe.accounts.unsupported' : 'moe.accounts.notConnected') }].
3. Otherwise, with now = clock.now() and zone = clock.zone():
   - description = the chips(rotation, now, zone) list resolved and joined with SEPARATOR inside text('moe.accounts.header', joined), or undefined when there are no chips;
   - message = rotation.error ? text('moe.accounts.error', rotation.error) : rotation.cli ? undefined : text('moe.accounts.noCli');
   - items = rows(rotation, now, zone) mapped to { id: row.id, contextValue: 'moe.account', label: `${row.position}. ${row.label}`, description, tooltip }:
     - description = `${resolve(status)} · ${text('moe.accounts.column.fiveHour')}: ${resolve(fiveHour)} · ${text('moe.accounts.column.weekly')}: ${resolve(weekly)}`;
     - tooltip = one `${column}: ${value}` line each for signIn, fiveHour, weekly, status and vmToken, joined with '\n';
   - when there are no rows: [] if rotation.error (the message carries it, as JetBrains leaves the table blank), else [{ label: text('moe.accounts.empty') }].
Methods:
- getChildren(node) returns node ? [] : parts().items.
- getTreeItem(node) returns a vscode.TreeItem(node.label, None) with id, description, tooltip and contextValue copied.
- attach(view: { description?: string; message?: string }) stores the TreeView, then applies parts().description and .message to it.
- refresh() is a no-op once disposed; otherwise it re-applies the view parts and fires onDidChangeTreeData. It also re-renders relative reset times.
- dispose() disposes the three subscriptions and the emitter, and drops the view.
Error handling:
- every input is total, because parseAccountRotation, rows and chips (VSC-13) never throw;
- a missing or malformed rotation renders a state item;
- an unknown local zone falls back to 'UTC' (VSC-13's time() also catches RangeError);
- refresh after dispose touches nothing.
implementationPlan.note: Created AccountsTreeProvider.ts (Write tool) per plan: type-only client import, constructor(client, clock?), parts(), getChildren, getTreeItem, attach(view), refresh(), dispose(). attach takes Pick<vscode.TreeView, 'description'|'message'> so a real TreeView (message: string|MarkdownString) type-checks. Compile verified in the step 6 snapshot gate.

implementationPlan.description:
Create moe-vscode/tests/accounts-view.test.cjs with the Write tool. Use 'use strict', node:test, node:assert/strict, node:vm, fs, path and typescript.
Loading:
- AccountPresentation.ts: as tests/managed-vm.test.cjs loads a pure module, via transpile then vm.runInThisContext of the (exports, module, require) wrapper, with a require that throws.
- AccountsTreeProvider.ts: the same way, but with require mapping 'vscode' to a fake and '../util/AccountPresentation' to that module. Any other name throws, which proves the client import is type-only.
- Fake vscode:
  - an EventEmitter whose event(listener) adds to a Set and returns { dispose } that deletes it, with fire() and dispose();
  - a TreeItem class storing label and collapsibleState;
  - TreeItemCollapsibleState { None: 0 }.
- Fake client: { connectionState, isStateReady, accountRotation, onAccountsChanged, onConnectionChanged, onStateChanged }, each event from its own fake emitter, so listener counts can be read.
- en(text): parse moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties with /^(moe\.[A-Za-z.]+)=(.*?)\r?$/gm, take the key's value (fail if it is missing) and substitute each {n} with String(args[n]).
- Corpus: moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-accounts.json (VSC-7, unchanged). Construct the provider with { now: () => Date.parse(corpus.now), zone: () => corpus.zone }.
Tests:
- P1 (DoD 1): package.json has views.moe { id 'moe.accounts', name equal to the bundle's moe.accounts.title }, the moe.accounts.refresh command with icon $(refresh), and a view/title entry { command 'moe.accounts.refresh', when 'view == moe.accounts', group 'navigation@1' }.
- V1 (DoD 2):
  - Take row C05, asserting it exists with at least 2 accounts. Set rotation = { ...C05.rotation, accounts: first two } and expected = C05.expectRows.slice(0, 2).
  - getChildren() returns exactly 2 nodes, in order.
  - getTreeItem gives label `${e.position}. ${e.label}`, id e.id and contextValue 'moe.account'.
  - description is `${en(e.status)} · ${en(column.fiveHour)}: ${en(e.fiveHour)} · ${en(column.weekly)}: ${en(e.weekly)}`.
  - tooltip is the five `${en(column.X)}: ${en(e.X)}` lines.
  - With the full C05 rotation, attach(view) sets view.description to en(header, [C05.expectChips.map(en).join('  ·  ')]).
- V2 (DoD 3):
  - firing each of the three client events fires onDidChangeTreeData exactly once;
  - disconnected gives exactly [notConnected];
  - connected with isStateReady and a null rotation gives exactly [unsupported]; connected without state ready gives [notConnected];
  - C02 gives exactly [empty];
  - C03 gives [] and view.message = en(error, [C03.rotation.error]);
  - C11 has rows, and view.message = en(noCli);
  - after dispose(), every client emitter has 0 listeners, and a later client event fires nothing.
- X1 (DoD 4): read src/extension.ts as text and match the four lines from step 4, each inside context.subscriptions.push or attach.
Error handling: an unreadable bundle, corpus or source fails with its path. Compare vm values field by field or through JSON.
Iterate with `cd moe-vscode && node --test tests/accounts-view.test.cjs`, using plain node; never run npm in the shared checkout.

(1) Scratch sweep of 24 mutants in the throwaway gate snapshot (driver /tmp/vsc14-mutants/mutate.cjs): the 6 planned (drop onStateChanged, unsupported before isStateReady, listener left undisposed, swapped 5-hour/weekly, row for an error rotation, chips joined with ' · ') plus 18 more (dropped connection/accounts subscriptions, unguarded refresh/attach after dispose, wrong contextValue, children for a child node, 'connecting' as connected, blank description, refresh skipping apply, tooltip join, inverted noCli, emitter not disposed, id/position dropped, error text dropped, empty-state removed) — 23 KILLED by accounts-view assertions; 1 ALIVE = 'dispose twice allowed', an equivalent mutant (every disposer and emitter.dispose is idempotent, so a second dispose is unobservable). (2) V5 pins no-throw for hostile rotation, missing cli, error rotation, unknown zone, local clock. (3) V6: refresh/attach after dispose fire and touch nothing (late-fire counter on the disposed emitter). (4) ids = account ids, unique because parseAccountRotation keeps the first duplicate. (6) Diff = exactly the five planned files (~350 net changed lines, under the 400 cap). Considered, theoretical: onStateChanged fires on every board delta, so refresh re-sets view.description/message each time (same churn as ManagedVmTreeProvider's onStateChanged fire; 32 accounts max); a throwing client event registration in the constructor would leak the earlier subscriptions (the client always has all three events). Known deviation from JetBrains, as the DoD asks: disconnected shows the state item, not stale rows.
